one_liner: Entry-to-mid budget analyst at NGA, an intelligence agency, building, tracking and defending budgets in the Pentagon's PPBE process; requires TS/SCI with polygraph.
fit_summary: The job is open to the public, and your IEM work with government clients may give useful exposure to how public programs are funded. However, all four mandatory criteria require hands-on budget execution or formulation, financial systems and spreadsheet work, and financial problem-solving, and none of that is documented for you yet. Your policy knowledge and people skills help with the 'present, defend, communicate' parts of the role, but they will not get you past the mandatory screen alone.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens); no prior federal status is needed.

Education: a bachelor's in accounting, business, finance, public administration or a related field, OR 24 semester hours in those areas plus experience totaling 4 years, OR 4 years of accounting, budget or financial analysis experience.

Your resume must show specific examples and results for each of the four Mandatory Qualification Criteria: financial corrective actions, budget inquiries, financial databases and spreadsheets, and budget execution or formulation.
You must be able to obtain a Top Secret/SCI clearance and pass a counterintelligence polygraph and drug test, with annual financial disclosure (SF-714).
strategy: Pull together exactly what you did at IEM involving money, such as contract or task-order budgets, burn-rate tracking, FEMA Public Assistance or grant cost documentation, invoices, or cost estimates. Map each item to one of the four mandatory criteria; if you can't fill all four honestly, this posting is a long shot.
Use the NGA resume builder and stay within 2 pages. Give each relevant job dates and hours per week, and write one or two result-focused bullets per mandatory criterion using the posting's wording.

Frame your emergency-management consulting as financial work for government clients, for example 'analyzed disaster recovery cost estimates for [client agency]'. Mention policy knowledge only where it supports interpreting budget laws, regulations or appropriations.
State your degree and major clearly, along with any accounting, finance or public-administration coursework hours, so HR can confirm option A or B.
Attach a short optional cover letter connecting your government-client work to federal budget execution and expressing willingness to complete TS/SCI processing.
Apply between Oct 19 and Oct 31, 2026, and don't wait for the last day; hiring-event postings can fill quickly.
resume_bullets: Tracked [budget/contract value] for [number] [FEMA/state/local] disaster recovery task orders in [Excel/system], reconciling obligations against spending [frequency] and flagging [issue type] to project leads.
Researched and drafted responses to [number] budget and cost inquiries from [client agency] staff, coordinating with [teams] to recommend [corrective action/solution] that [result].
Prepared cost estimates and justifications for [project/proposal] totaling [amount], consolidating inputs from [number] sources into [document type] for client review.
interview_questions: Tell us about a time you identified a financial problem and recommended a corrective action. What happened?
How would you explain a budget variance or funds request to a senior leader who disagrees with your analysis?
Which financial systems or spreadsheet tools have you used, and how did you use them to track execution?
What do you know about the PPBE process, and how does budget execution differ from formulation?
watch_outs: The TS/SCI clearance with polygraph can take many months, and your finances (debts, missed payments) will be scrutinized.
You can't telework, you could be placed in multiple locations (likely Springfield, VA or St. Louis), and your specific assignment may change after you clear.

Without documented budget or financial experience you are likely to be screened out at the mandatory-criteria stage. A budget- or program-analyst role closer to emergency management, such as at FEMA, state VDEM, or Prince William County, may fit you better.
